pre-commit.description: Renovate's pre-commit manager is opt-in. Without this the hook revisions in .pre-commit-config.yaml are the one dependency file nobody is watching.

packageRules.description: Minor, patch and digest updates are not merged automatically: every update needs review
Major updates are batched into the first day of each month rather than arriving in the weekly window, so the disruptive changes are looked at deliberately and at most once a month.
schedule: on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: CI tooling (GitHub Actions and pre-commit hook revisions) moves in one monthly pull request covering every update type, digests included, instead of a stream of small ones. A security fix for any of these still arrives at once, because vulnerability alerts ignore the schedule and grouping.
schedule: on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: A Renovate major can raise engines.node past the node-version that .github/workflows/renovate.yml sets up, leaving every hourly run on a Node that Renovate does not support. This note reaches the reviewer of the bump.
prBodyNotes: :warning: Before merging, check this version's `engines.node` (`npm view renovate@<version> engines`) against `node-version` in `.github/workflows/renovate-fleet.yml` and `.github/workflows/renovate.yml`. If it no longer accepts that Node major, raise `node-version` in the same pull request in both, and in shakenfist/development's `templates/renovate/renovate.yml`, which every repository copies verbatim.

packageRules.description: Renovate's github-actions manager proposes Node majors for setup-node, and .github/workflows/renovate-fleet.yml and .github/workflows/renovate.yml must stay on a Node that the pinned Renovate's engines.node accepts, or every hourly run fails with "Unsupported node environment detected". That Node is raised by hand, in the pull request for the Renovate major that needs it (see the rule above), never on its own. The first and last file names exist only in shakenfist/development, which runs the central runner and ships that template to the rest of the fleet, and are inert everywhere else. Node in other workflows is unaffected.

shellcheck-py tags a fourth packaging component -- v0.11.0.1 is shellcheck 0.11.0, packaging revision 1 -- which is not semver, so without this the github-tags lookup behind the pre-commit hook fails with "Can't find version matching" on the dependency dashboard and no update is ever proposed. The fourth group is named build rather than revision: Renovate's regex versioning only compares revision when a build group matched too, so naming it revision would make v0.11.0.2 compare equal to v0.11.0.1 and hide packaging-only releases. The anchor to exactly four numeric components ignores re-tags such as v0.11.0.1-1. Harmless in a repository that does not use the hook. See templates/renovate/README.md in shakenfist/development.
